transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

What scared me enough to come in is that at work, during quiet stretches in the surveillance room, I hear voices through the monitor speakers. They say things like, “You missed it, Ruth,” or, “People are going to get hurt because of you,” even when every channel is muted. Nobody else hears them.
About how long have you been hearing these voices?
About four months now—since I was moved into the lead surveillance role at the casino.
How has your mood been over these past four months?
Most days, I feel this heavy gray mood before I even get out of bed. It just hangs over me. I’ve found myself tearing up in my car before a shift over something as small as seeing the casino lights.
Have you had any periods during these past four months when your mood felt back to normal, but you were still hearing the voices?

No. I haven’t had a time where I felt normal again and the voices kept happening. They started with this whole low, guilty period after the lead change, and they seem tied together. Before that, I’d never heard things through the equipment or felt like I was dangerous to everyone.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt the opposite—extremely energetic, needing very little sleep, or having your thoughts racing?
I don’t think so. I can’t remember a time when I felt unusually energetic or like I didn’t need sleep.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe depressive episode lasting four months characterized by pervasive low mood, tearfulness, and feelings of guilt, accompanied by mood-congruent auditory hallucinations. The psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the depressive episode without independent psychotic periods or a history of manic episodes, fulfilling criteria for a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.
